questions.q: Which groups did Mao focus on to build his base of support?
a: Peasants and women, whom he courted publicly
Urban factory owners and foreign investors
Students and military officers in coastal cities
Religious leaders and the old aristocracy
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Mao turned his back on the rich and built communism by appealing to peasants, then women.

questions.q: How did Mao present himself to the Chinese public?
a: As one of the crowd who understood their struggles but could fix them
As a distant intellectual who had studied abroad
As a reluctant leader who disliked holding power
As a wealthy patron who would share his fortune
questions.why: The overview describes him showing a positive side and appearing connected to ordinary people yet strong enough to solve their problems.

questions.q: Why did Mao order a billion copies of the Little Red Book printed?
a: To spread his personality cult and popularity at home and abroad
To provide free reading material for Chinese schoolchildren
To replace all other books in Chinese libraries
To raise money for industrial development
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the compilation of his quotations was meant to increase his popularity as a communist leader.

questions.q: What happened when Mao tried to help the Indonesian Communist Party take over?
a: The attempt failed and roughly half a million people were killed
The party succeeded and Indonesia adopted Maoism
The army joined the party and shared power peacefully
The plan was abandoned before any violence occurred
questions.why: Lesson 2 recounts the failed attempt and the mass killing that followed when the army suppressed the movement.

questions.q: What happened in Tanzania after its leader adopted Mao’s model?
a: Nationalizing industry and pushing farming led to poverty and famine
The country quickly became an industrial powerhouse
Living standards rose steadily for the whole population
The plan was reversed before it affected the economy
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the Tanzanian leader’s Mao-inspired transformation produced poverty and famine.
